AI companies have spent years scraping images, voices, writing, and other content from the internet to train their models. Now artists, photographers, writers, and ordinary users are starting to fight back by turning the very data those systems collect into a trap.

This video explores tools like Glaze and Nightshade, which subtly modify images so they look normal to humans while confusing the AI models that train on them. Researchers have shown that just a small number of poisoned images can corrupt individual concepts, causing models to generate distorted animals, confuse objects, and eventually degrade the quality of their own output.
